utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-96-21-A bis, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Mucic, Hazim Delic, and Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may it please you, I appear on behalf of the Prosecution. My name is Anthony Carmona. Ms. Helen Brady appears with me, and Mr. Wolfgang Zakalic is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: For Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Tomislav Kuzmanovic on behalf of Mr. Mucic. Mr. Morrison has other professional commitments in England.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: For Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Salih Karabdic, an attorney from Sarajevo, and I'm here with my co-counsel, Mr. Thomas Moran, on behalf of Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. I am Cynthia Sinatra for Mr. Landzo, along with associate counsel, Mr. Peter Murphy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference which has been called in accordance with the Rules. We're not at any stage of the proceedings that we can deal with the issues arising out of those. Well, not many of them anyway. Is there anything that any counsel wishes to raise on behalf of their client, the other matters to which the Status Conference Rule refers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have just a question regarding the briefing. The Scheduling Order required that the OTP file a brief by 14 February 2002, and as of today none of the Defence lawyers have received a copy. I understand there's been an amendment to the Rules dealing with the timing of filing of briefs, and we had a discussion amongst ourselves and amongst the OTP, and we'd like to come to some resolution on when we are going to be expecting a response brief, because the 24 December 2001 Scheduling Order says the consolidated respondent's brief shall be filed no later than 14 February 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I probably signed it, but I have absolutely no recollection of it, Mr. Kuzmanovic. But according to the legal officer's computations, the respondent has 40 days to respond and that is until the 24th of February, which is a Sunday, so that we would expect their response by next Monday. But anyway, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can give the assurance that we in fact would file by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. And then the reply would follow in accordance with the new Rules. There seems to be an epidemic of instances over the last few months where the counsel have somewhat disregarded their obligations in a reply, and they seek to go off onto new paths, raise new grounds of appeal, and all sorts of things. Those attempts are not being treated with very much sympathy. If you want to raise something new, then it must be raised in your appellant's brief and by leave, and if there are matters which are inserted in a reply which are not a reply to the response, you may find there will be an order striking them out. Now, the one issue -- I'm sorry. That's for Mr. Kuzmanovic. Anything from you, Mr. Karabdic, that you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we have anything to raise, except that there's a possibility --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we have anything to raise, except there's a possibility for oral argument, that I may have a very important personal commitment in the middle of May, and if you want me to bring that forward --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I hope that we'll be hearing this before May, but then one never knows. But whilst you're on your feet, Mr. Moran, the application which you have filed on behalf of your client for a review should have never been filed in this reply. It's a completely separate proceeding and has been recently given a new number by the Registry, so that it has been hived off, as it were, from the appeal. Obviously it will have to be heard or disposed of before the sentence appeal is dealt with. I understand that the President is today assigning Judges to hear the review. But having read the papers, assuming that I have got something to do with it, you might like to tell me what your attitude is towards this document which the whole of your review depends upon and which the Prosecution has sought to establish was in your client's possession during the course of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Karabdic would be the appropriate person to speak to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Karabdic, the reply which you have filed does not in any way seek to deny what is said by the Prosecution, although there's a somewhat strange statement on an unnumbered page, which was page 5 of the fax: "That does not mean that Delic admits the new fact was available before and be discoverable through the exercise of due diligence. Let the Prosecutor prove that if she wish, but that will be unuseful spending of time, Delic thinks." Now, we've got material before us which has your signature on it which demonstrates that you had this statement during the course of the trial. How can this review proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are signatures showing that I received some witness statements; however, it cannot be concluded from them that I received both statements. That's one thing. Another is that I based my application for a review on the fact that there is an issue that significantly affects the decision and indicates that a miscarriage of justice must be avoided. In the interests of justice, the application should be granted, because if this is accepted, it will lead to a completely different judgement than the previous one. I believe that the Defence has the right to rely on this, just as the Prosecutor relied on this before the Rwanda Tribunal, and I think that the right to apply for a review belongs also to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the right to a review is provided for by Statute and it does require you to produce a fact which was not known to you and which was not discoverable by due diligence. Now, I do not understand how we have jurisdiction to hear a review if you cannot establish that fact. But if you are relying upon something else, no doubt you will produce some authorities in support of your proposition. I'm not sure where you'll get them from. You realise, don't you, that there has been a request from the Appeals Chamber to the Prosecution to elaborate that response about the two documents, and on the 8th of February there was a Prosecution's response to that request for further information which, on the face of it, seems to deal, very elaborately and very definitively, with any argument that you did not receive the particular statement upon which you rely. Now, if you want to rely to that, you can. I suggest that if you can, you should. Do you wish to file a reply to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Certainly, I do. I can say now that in my view, the response of the Prosecution is not truly a response to the request made of the Appeals Chamber. The Prosecution has not given a proper response, and I will elaborate on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I can't make an order at this moment, because I have not formally been assigned to the review. But assuming that that is signed today, I will make an order within the next couple of days. How long do you need in which to respond to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I will make a note on that. And if I am not on the review, I will speak to the Judge who will be the pre-hearing Judge for that and you will have that leave. Right. Now, is there anything else that anybody wants to raise in accordance with the Rule relating to Status Conferences? Ms. Sinatra, do you wish to raise anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We were just curious about the status of the Prosecution's reply brief, and I thought it might be useful to use this time to issue -- to talk to the Court about a new Scheduling Order, if that were possible, based upon the new amended Rules and maybe so that we could all anticipate a time for oral argument in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, at the moment that you've finished your filings, we'll consult you in relation to an appropriate date, and we will take into account Mr. Moran's problems. Just a moment. I'll check what the new Rules say. I'm never quite sure that I've got the right copy here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I think we have 15 days to file a response to the Prosecution's response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The 15-day period is still there for the reply. So that will be -- take you through until -- through to about the 11th or the 12th of March. Mid-March, in other words. At the moment, we see the replies and then we have to dispose of the review that Mr. Delic has raised. So you'll be consulted at that stage when we dispose of that and we know precisely what is happening and how long it is likely to take for the hearing. But I should make it clear that as far as I can see, there is no right of any of the parties to try and relitigate matters which were litigated in the conviction appeal, and yet each of you appear to have attempted to do so. That is disposed of. We are hearing a sentence appeal, and it is not any part of our remit to hear matters which go to conviction. So if I were you, I would not spend too much time trying to argue matters which go to conviction. As to the jurisdiction to have this matter determined by a fresh Trial Chamber, I suggest to you that is a matter that was dealt with in the conviction appeal, and having been dealt with, it's not open to be re-argued. That may be subject to anything which my colleagues will say, but that's my view of it. We are here to hear a sentence appeal from a very limited re-sentencing, a re-sentencing which was directed to deal with the fact that there were less convictions and some other very limited matters particularly relating to Mr. Delic and the fact that one of his other convictions was removed as well. So as a hearing, it should not take very long. Right. Now, anything the Prosecution wants to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Carmona.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wish to bring to the attention the fact that we had made a request for the book of authorities from Mr. Kuzmanovic. In fact, we had relayed our concern that the book of authorities was not filed. And in the context of the pending appeal, as much as, in fact, the utility of his proffering those book of authorities now may be lost, certainly in the context of the appeal, we certainly would prefer if, in fact, such book of authorities can, in fact, be sent to us or can be filed. In any event, as much as, in fact, we have had to look at his authorities, we do have most of it. And I can assure you, Your Honour, that it is our intention to liaise possibly with Mr. Kuzmanovic to determine exactly what we are missing, although it would certainly help us, it will help the Court, if an entire book of authorities probably is filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I haven't had the opportunity of reading the appeal. Are there a lot of authorities which are not familiar to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: They are from the American jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh. We're familiar with a few of those. Anyway, I see the problem, because we certainly don't have access to the American authorities. What about it, Mr. Kuzmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not a problem. I have replied to an e-mail notifying that if the cases that I've cited need to be filed and served, I will certainly do so. All of them are available on the Internet at no cost, but I will surely provide opposing counsel and the Court, if the Court so desires, with a copy of all the cases that I've cited in our brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are the Internet versions paginated the same as the printed versions of the reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably. Some of them are. Some of they aren't, Your Honour. I think if you're on something like Westlaw or Lexis they are. If you're on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Lexis is very good usually because they give you, in square brackets, the page of the actual report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will -- I will file them nonetheless, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It might be advisable. It would be very helpful. Anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. Well, we'll adjourn the Status Conference, and we'll let you know what date the hearing of the appeal will be.
